investigations.title: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
investigations.title_es: Análisis computacional y experimental de conjuntos de datos SPICE
investigations.sponsoring_agency: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) PSI grant
investigations.objective: This ground investigation sought to increase understanding of the issues that control the large discrepancy between soot formation in 1g and in 0g flames. The objective of this investigation was to integrate computational and experimental methods to derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment (SPICE) data available in PSI. By analyzing over 1600 raw DSLR images and incorporating advanced soot models, the study sought to improve understanding of soot formation, oxidation, radiative re-absorption, and aggregate growth in heavily sooting flames. The work further aimed to reconcile microgravity and normal gravity flame behavior, identify key physical and chemical processes influencing smoke point development, and provide a framework for evaluating model parameter sensitivity.
investigations.approach: The approach was to combine image processing, experimental diagnostics, and detailed soot modeling. Raw Nikon NEF images were decoded into three color channels and analyzed using color-ratio pyrometry to extract soot temperature fields. Absolute light calibration from SPICE was then used to calculate soot volume fractions. For computational modeling, a coupled flow–species–soot system was implemented, modified to include radiation re-absorption and discrete-sectional aggregate formation. Simulations were performed for both Yale and ACME burner configurations under normal and microgravity conditions. Comparisons between experimental data and computed results guided sensitivity analyses of soot evolution parameters, including the effects of radiation, scattering, boundary conditions, and heat transfer to the burner structure.
investigations.research_impacts: This study sought to enhance understanding of soot formation, flame structure, and radiative transport under microgravity and normal gravity, improving predictive models for combustion in both spacecraft and terrestrial systems. For space applications, the results support safer fire detection, suppression, and cleaner combustion technologies critical for long-duration missions. On Earth, the insights help reduce pollutant emissions, optimize combustion efficiency, and inform the design of cleaner energy and industrial systems.

investigations.summary_es: Esta investigación terrestre buscó aumentar la comprensión de los problemas que controlan la gran discrepancia entre la formación de hollín en llamas de 1 gy 0 g. El objetivo de esta investigación fue integrar métodos computacionales y experimentales para derivar distribuciones de temperatura y fracciones de volumen de hollín a partir de los datos del Experimento de punto de humo en coflujo (SPICE) disponibles en PSI. Este estudio buscó mejorar la comprensión de la formación de hollín, la estructura de la llama y el transporte radiativo en condiciones de microgravedad y gravedad normal, mejorando los modelos predictivos de combustión tanto en naves espaciales como en sistemas terrestres.
key_findings: The study re-analyzed more than 1,600 raw SPICE DSLR images with color-ratio pyrometry to derive soot temperature fields and, after absolute light calibration, soot volume fractions.
It coupled flow, species, and soot modeling with radiation re-absorption and discrete-sectional aggregate formation for Yale and ACME burners in normal and microgravity conditions.
Sensitivity analyses identified how radiation, scattering, boundary conditions, and burner heat transfer affect soot evolution and the interpretation of smoke-point data.
key_findings_es: El estudio reanalizó más de 1.600 imágenes DSLR crudas de SPICE con pirometría de relación de colores para derivar campos de temperatura de hollín y, tras calibración absoluta de luz, fracciones volumétricas de hollín.
Acopló modelos de flujo, especies y hollín con reabsorción de radiación y formación de agregados por secciones discretas para quemadores Yale y ACME en condiciones de gravedad normal y microgravedad.

Los análisis de sensibilidad identificaron cómo la radiación, la dispersión, las condiciones de contorno y la transferencia de calor al quemador afectan la evolución del hollín y la interpretación de los datos de punto de humo.
limitations: Color-ratio pyrometry depends on emissivity and calibration assumptions, and the analysis is a ground-based re-use of archival images rather than a new experiment.
The public record does not provide the derived soot fields or the model sensitivity tables.
limitations_es: La pirometría de relación de colores depende de supuestos de emisividad y calibración, y el análisis es una reutilización en tierra de imágenes de archivo, no un experimento nuevo.
El registro público no proporciona los campos de hollín derivados ni las tablas de sensibilidad del modelo.

investigations.title: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
investigations.title_es: Efecto de la perturbación termoconvectiva externa en la dinámica de la llama fría: un análisis CFD multidimensional y multifísico
investigations.sponsoring_agency: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) PSI grant
investigations.objective: The objective of this ground investigation was to use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA’s Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of already established droplet cool flames, and to explain run-to-run variability by isolating the roles of deliberate heating and unintentional drift-induced convection. Focusing on both small and large droplets, the work mapped stability windows for ignition, sustained oscillation, transitions to hot ignition and warm-flame behavior, and extinction under microgravity. By leveraging and extending the FLEX data in the PSI, this study produced reusable models and sensitivity analyses that coupled low-temperature chemistry with transport and radiative effects.
investigations.approach:
OpenFOAM was used to develop a 3-D CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier–Stokes flow with low-temperature combustion chemistry, coupled heat and mass transfer, and radiation. Model fidelity was established against ISS FLEX measurements, after which controlled simulations examined three forcing modes (i) convection alone to mimic droplet drift, (ii) imposed heat flux, and (iii) combined convection plus heating applied to both large (1–4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplets.

To accelerate progress, the study began with simplified chemistry and transitioned to reduced mechanisms for parameter sweeps over forcing amplitude and frequency, ambient composition (including ozone-assisted cases), and pressure. From each case, predictive observables were extracted (ignition delay, oscillation frequency and amplitude, stand-off and extinction diameters), and were used to construct stability maps that delineated conditions for cool-flame onset, persistence, and quenching. These maps were reconciled with FLEX observations and were used to guide next-generation test matrices for both large- and small-droplet experiments.
investigations.research_impacts:
Space Benefits: Potential to improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling by resolving cool-flame/extinction behavior in microgravity; leverages FLEX to define safer operating envelopes/materials.
Earth Benefits: Advances low-temperature combustion understanding relevant to engine knock, efficiency, and emissions; delivers validated CFD tools transferrable to practical combustors.

Space Benefits: Potential to improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling by resolving cool-flame/extinction behavior in microgravity; leverages FLEX to define safer operating envelopes/materials.
investigations.summary_es: El objetivo de esta investigación terrestre fue utilizar datos de vuelo obtenidos de PSI a través del Experimento de Extinción de Llamas (FLEX) de la NASA para cuantificar cómo las perturbaciones térmicas y convectivas impuestas externamente regulaban la dinámica y el destino final de las llamas frías de gotas ya establecidas, y para explicar la variabilidad entre ejes aislando los roles del calentamiento deliberado y la convección inducida por la deriva no intencional. Centrándose en gotas tanto pequeñas como grandes, el trabajo trazó ventanas de estabilidad para la ignición, la oscilación sostenida, las transiciones a la ignición caliente y al comportamiento de llama cálida, y la extinción bajo microgravedad. Beneficios espaciales: Potencial para mejorar el modelado de seguridad contra incendios de naves espaciales al resolver el comportamiento de llama fría/extinción en microgravedad; aprovecha FLEX para definir envolventes/materiales operativos más seguros.
key_findings: The study built a three-dimensional OpenFOAM model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density flow, low-temperature chemistry, heat and mass transfer, and radiation.

After anchoring the model to FLEX measurements, it mapped stability windows for ignition, sustained oscillation, hot ignition, warm-flame behavior, and extinction under convection, heating, and combined forcing.

The extracted observables—ignition delay, oscillation frequency and amplitude, stand-off and extinction diameters—provide a basis for safer spacecraft fire-safety envelopes and next-generation test matrices.
key_findings_es: El estudio construyó un modelo tridimensional en OpenFOAM de llamas frías de gotas de n-alcano en microgravedad, acoplando flujo de densidad variable, química de baja temperatura, transferencia de calor y masa, y radiación.

Tras anclar el modelo a las mediciones de FLEX, mapeó ventanas de estabilidad para ignición, oscilación sostenida, ignición caliente, comportamiento de llama tibia y extinción bajo convección, calentamiento y forzamiento combinado.

Los observables extraídos —retardo de ignición, frecuencia y amplitud de oscilación, diámetros de separación y extinción— sirven de base para envolventes de seguridad contra incendios y nuevas matrices de ensayo.
limitations: The conclusions depend on reduced chemical mechanisms and on the fidelity of the FLEX dataset; model uncertainty is not fully characterized in the public summary.
The work is a ground-based CFD analysis, not a new microgravity experiment, so its stability maps still require flight validation.
limitations_es: Las conclusiones dependen de mecanismos químicos reducidos y de la fidelidad del conjunto de datos FLEX; la incertidumbre del modelo no se caracteriza por completo en el resumen público.
El trabajo es un análisis CFD en tierra, no un nuevo experimento en microgravedad, por lo que sus mapas de estabilidad aún requieren validación en vuelo.

investigations.title: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
investigations.title_es: Utilización de los datos del experimento de medición de aerosoles de humo para el modelado avanzado y la simulación de la generación de humo en microgravedad
investigations.sponsoring_agency: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) PSI Grant
investigations.objective: The objective of this investigation was to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth from a fundamental perspective. The intention of this effort is to quantify the differences between microgravity and Earth gravity smoke, and to identify the fluid dynamic mechanisms that cause the differences.
investigations.approach: The formation and growth of dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) particles in Earth gravity and microgravity environments was simulated. Direct numerical simulation via a Navier-Stokes nodal approach was utlilized. The smoke originates from pyrolysis vapor expelled from a heated sample in a geometry similar to that considered in the SAME experiments. This study considered two cross-flow velocities of sufficiently low speed that buoyancy cannot be neglected in the presence of gravity. Simulations are presented to assess the dependence of particle size distributions on thermophoresis, particle settling, and flow geometry. The final report for this investigation introduces the simulation and modeling methodology, followed by a description of the flow geometry and the parameter space under consideration.The differences in the wake geometry attributable to buoyancy for the lower of two flow speeds was examined. Instantaneous scalar fields were used to describe particle accumulation and growth in the buoyant and non-buoyant wakes that form downstream of the hot vapor source.
investigations.research_impacts: Models and tools that characterize particles generated as smoke can be used to ascertain how temperature, gravity, and material properties affect the smoke produced. This would directly lead to better smoke detection devices and prevent fires that can lead to loss of materiel and loss of life.
investigations.summary_en: The objective of this investigation was to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth from a fundamental perspective. The intention of this effort is to quantify the differences between microgravity and Earth gravity smoke, and to identify the fluid dynamic mechanisms that cause the differences. Models and tools that characterize particles generated as smoke can be used to ascertain how temperature, gravity, and material properties affect the smoke produced.
investigations.summary_es: El objetivo de esta investigación fue utilizar simulación numérica para explorar la influencia de la gravedad en el crecimiento del humo de pirólisis desde una perspectiva fundamental. La intención de este esfuerzo es cuantificar las diferencias entre la microgravedad y el humo de la gravedad de la Tierra, e identificar los mecanismos fluidodinámicos que causan las diferencias. Se pueden utilizar modelos y herramientas que caracterizan las partículas generadas como humo para determinar cómo la temperatura, la gravedad y las propiedades del material afectan el humo producido.
key_findings: The study simulated dibutyl-phthalate smoke growth in Earth gravity and microgravity using a Navier-Stokes nodal approach and a geometry representative of the SAME experiment.
It isolated the roles of thermophoresis, particle settling, and wake geometry, and showed how buoyancy changes particle accumulation downstream of the hot vapor source.
The resulting models and tools connect temperature, gravity, and material properties to smoke characteristics, with direct application to smoke-detection design.
key_findings_es: El estudio simuló el crecimiento de humo de dibutilftalato en gravedad terrestre y microgravedad mediante un enfoque nodal de Navier-Stokes y una geometría representativa del experimento SAME.

Aisló el papel de la termoforesis, la sedimentación de partículas y la geometría de la estela, y mostró cómo la flotabilidad modifica la acumulación de partículas aguas abajo de la fuente de vapor caliente.
Los modelos y herramientas resultantes conectan temperatura, gravedad y propiedades del material con las características del humo, con aplicación directa al diseño de detectores.
limitations: This is a ground-based numerical study using a single surrogate fuel and simplified geometry; experimental validation across materials is still required.
The public record does not provide the simulated particle-size distributions or a reusable dataset.
limitations_es: Se trata de un estudio numérico en tierra con un único combustible sustituto y geometría simplificada; aún se requiere validación experimental con distintos materiales.
El registro público no proporciona las distribuciones simuladas de tamaño de partícula ni un conjunto de datos reutilizable.
